data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate showed a gross prior-year deterioration of approximately $64.0m (about 22.9% of opening gross claims reserves) for accident years up to 2018. This adverse movement was driven by reserve strengthening across multiple older underwriting years, with notable catastrophe impacts (Hurricanes Florence and Michael) and COVID-19 related deterioration on closed years (including 2017 YoA). The syndicate narrative also reports a small prior-accident-year adverse development on a claims-incurred basis ($1.1m) and net COVID losses reported in various classes, reflecting differences between net (after reinsurance) and gross measures.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (63.974m) was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross cumulative estimates, USD thousands  converted to millions). The report also contains narrative and P&L statements that cite a much smaller prior-year adverse 'claims incurred' figure ($1.1m) which is a P&L (claims incurred) measure and may be net of reinsurance; these are different concepts (gross reserve re-estimation vs claims-incurred movement). Some COVID figures quoted in the text are described as 'net' after reinsurance and/or refer to particular years of account; where only net amounts were provided the gross split by LOB is not available. Mapping of 'Crisis Management' / 'Contingency' impacts to the standard Lloyd's LOBs was not explicit; LOB-level prior year movements are not quantified in the report and are therefore mostly null or low confidence.
